overview.body:
**Sarnath** ​(*sarnath*) ‌— First ‌Sermon, ​Deer ​Park · ​Lord ​of ​the deer ‌— ​belongs ​to the ‌Buddhist ​tradition, ‌where it ​is ‌catalogued ​under the ​domain ​"First ​Sermon, Deer ​Park". ‌The ​name means ‌"Lord ​of ‌the deer".

​**Sarnath** ‌is ​first sermon, ‌deer ​park. ​The name ‌means ‌"Lord ‌of the ​deer" ​and ‌belongs to ​the ​buddhist ‌tradition.

PuniCodex ​restores ​the ‌name as ​**Sarnath** ‌and ​serves its ​temple ​at ​[its temple](https://punicodex.com/sarnath/). ‌The ‌restoration ​needs no ‌distinctive ​letters ​or diacritics ‌its ‌ASCII ‌form would ‌lose, ​which ‌places the ​name ​in ​Tier 2. ‌The ​plain ​ASCII form ​*sarnath* ‌survives ​as a ​modern ​convenience ‌imposed by ​the ‌early ​domain-name system; ‌the ​restoration, ‌not the ‌fallback, ​is ​the form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in ​Devanagari as ​**सर्नथ्**. ​Etymologically it ​means ​"Lord ‌of the ​deer".

​The ASCII ‌form ​*sarnath* ‌survives only ​because ‌the early ​domain-name ​system ​could not ​carry ​diacritics; it ‌is ​a ‌technological compromise, ​not ‌an ancient ​spelling. ‌The ​Unicode restoration ‌**Sarnath** ​recovers the ​full ‌diacritic ‌detail of ‌the ​scholarly transliteration ​directly ‌in ​the address ​bar. ‌The restoration ​needs ​no ‌distinctive letters ​or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ​form ​would lose, ​which ‌places ‌the name ​in ‌Tier 2.

​The ​letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

‌- ‌**s** → ‌**S** ​— ‌Same, capitalized
​- ​**a** → ​**a** ‌— ​Same
- ​**r** ​→ **r** ‌— ​Same
​- **n** ​→ ‌**n** — ​Same
‌- ​**a** → ‌**a** ​— Same
‌- ‌**t** ​→ **t** ​— ​Same
- ​**h** ‌→ ‌**h** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/sarnath/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**sarnath** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Sarnath.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"sarnath" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Sarnath".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"sarnath" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Sarnath" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Sarnath was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Sarnath ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Sarnath ‌place first ​sermon, ​deer ​park at ​the ​center of ‌a ​living mythological ​world.

‌### ​Origins (Myth)

‌Sarnath ​appears in ‌buddhist ​tradition as ​first ​sermon, ​deer park. ​The ‌name's meaning, ​"Lord ‌of the ​deer", ‌shapes ​the narratives ‌told ​about this ‌figure.

​### Worship ​and ‌Memory ‌(Cult)

Devotees ‌and ​later tradition-keepers ​preserved ‌Sarnath in ​ritual, ​text, ‌and iconography, ​ensuring ​the name ‌survived ​into the ‌modern ​scholarly record.

​The ​myths ​of Sarnath ‌survive ‌in fragments, ​summaries, ‌and later ​retellings. ​Each ‌version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ‌its ​tellers — ‌poets, ​priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ‌The PuniCodex ​entry ​does not ​privilege ‌a ​single version; ​it ​gathers the ‌attestations ​so that ‌readers ​can ‌compare them. ​The ‌restoration Sarnath ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable ​name around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or artifact ​in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet assigned ​to ‌Sarnath ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should be ​read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Buddhist ​name ‌of this ​type ‌the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected to ​be ​thin, ‌and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains the ‌textual ​testimony ​gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources section.

​Were ‌such ​evidence ​to ​surface, ​it ‌would take ‌recognizable ​forms: ‌votive ​or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming सर्नथ्, ‌sanctuary ‌or ​cult ‌remains ​tied ​to first ​sermon ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional ​attributes (name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be ‌weighed against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name ​before entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Sarnath is ‌to ​hold ​the idea ​of ​first ​Sermon, ‌Deer Park ​in ​the ‌mind and ​to ‌ask ​what ‌of it ​endures. ​The ​name means ​"Lord ​of ‌the ​deer" — ‌and ​a ‌name that ​carries ‌its ​meaning ‌so openly ​invites ​meditation ‌rather than ‌mere ‌recollection. ​The ​tradition remembers ‌the ​name ​as first ‌Sermon, ​Deer ​Park ‌· Lord ​of ‌the ​deer.

​Sit with ​the ​restored ‌form — ‌Sarnath ​— ‌and ​the diacritics ​themselves ‌become ‌the practice: ‌each ‌mark ​is ‌a small ​act ​of ​attention, a ‌refusal ​to ​let ​the plain ‌ASCII ​form ​*sarnath* stand ​in ‌for ​the ‌whole. What ​the ‌tradition ​preserved in ‌this ‌name, ​the ​restoration asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
